title: NEOWISE during ZTF dips shows small-grain extinction, not grey occultation, in 7 main-sequence dippers, and transient 4.6 um dust emission in the 2018 dip of a rapidly rotating K dwarf
abstract: Question: Are the dips of ZTF main-sequence dippers grey or chromatic to 4.6 um, and do these stars have warm dust more often than field stars? Approach: We used the 81 dipper candidates of Tzanidakis et al. (2025, TZ25) and 10 field-dwarf dimmers of prior campaign studies, 1,836 NEOWISE-R visits (2014-2024) and ZTF DR24 light curves. At each visit we measured the simultaneous ZTF drop and the field-calibrated infrared change, and we compared W1-W2 and 12 um detections with dwarf-matched controls from the same fields. Results: 29 visits of 19 stars fall in confirmed dips. For 7 TZ25 dippers (r drops 0.15-0.27 mag) the pooled ratio of W1 to r depth is 0.088 +- 0.052 (W2: 0.12 +- 0.09), so grey occultation by opaque bodies or large-grain discs is excluded at 17 sigma; campaign dimmers give 0.167 +- 0.020 and reproduce published values. TZ25 dippers have no W1-W2 or 12 um excess more often than controls (38 stars, KS p = 0.24). The deepest TZ25 dip, on Gaia DR3 2082534881979041280 (K2 dwarf, 335 pc, spot period 3.1 d, probably young), reached 4.9 mag in g in 2018. During it, W2 was 0.225 +- 0.026 mag brighter than quiet while r was 3.1 mag fainter; visits before and after are quiet. This needs dust emission of at least 0.6 percent of the stellar luminosity, about 1.6 percent at 1270 K for Gaia20cdd-like grains. Limitations: few and shallow in-dip visits, one infrared epoch for the emission, and an age from rotation only.
